# Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā (Atk S0509a)

**ID:** Atk S0509a
**Section:** Aṭṭhakathā Khuddakanikāya (atk-s05)
**Collection:** Atthakatha-Suttas
**Title (Pali):** Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā
**Title (English, from literature):** The Commentary on the Verses of the Therīs
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, titled *Paramatthadīpanī VI* and attributed to Ācariya Dhammapāla, is the Theravāda commentary on the *Therīgāthā* of the Khuddakanikāya [Carter 1978; Silk 2009; Skilling, Eṣā agrā]. Characterized as a skilful blend of bardic, philological, hermeneutic, and narrative genres, the work provides detailed biographical contexts and backstories explaining when and why the verses of the enlightened elder nuns (*therī*s) were uttered [Skilling, Eṣā agrā; Collett 2014]. In its legal and narrative discussions of monastic history, the commentary goes to great lengths to deny that direct ordination by the Buddha (*ehi* ordination) was ever granted to nuns, and it records ordination narratives where candidates are ordained by Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī without mentioning the presence of monks [Skilling, Eṣā agrā]. The text preserves significant variant narrative traditions, such as two differing accounts of the renunciation of Uppalavaṇṇā—one prompted by an overwhelming number of suitors, and a second involving marriage and double incest [Collett 2014].

To contextualize the biographies and past lives of the nuns, the commentary extensively quotes from the *Apadāna* [Norman, Philological Approach to Buddhism; Clark 2015]. Text-reuse data from DharmaNexus reflects this tight intertextual relationship, showing extensive reuse with the Apadāna poems of the nuns, including substantial shared passages with the *Mahāpajāpatigotamītherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 17), *Khemātherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 18), *Paṭācārātherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 20), *Kisāgotamītherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 22), and *Uppalavaṇṇātherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 19) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records thousands of matching segments with other commentarial works, especially Dhammapāla's *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Apadāna-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Aṅguttaranikāye Ekakanipāta-aṭṭhakathā*, and the *Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus].

A critical edition of the Pali text was prepared for the Pali Text Society by William Pruitt in 1998, accompanied by his complete English translation [Silk 2009; Skilling, Eṣā agrā; Clark 2015].

**Sources**

- [Carter 1978] John Ross Carter, Dhamma: Western Academic and Sinhalese Buddhist Interpretations (1978) — Identifies the commentary title Paramattha-Dīpanī Therīgāthā-Aṭṭhakathā.
- [Clark 2015] Chris Clark, A Study of the Apadāna, Including an Edition and Annotated Translation of the Second, Third, and Fourth Chapters (2015) — Discusses quotation of nuns' apadānas in the commentary and notes Pruitt's edition and translation.
- [Collett 2014] Alice Collett, ed., Women in Early Indian Buddhism: Comparative Textual Studies (2014) — Examines the commentary's narrative accounts of Uppalavaṇṇā's renunciation.
- [DharmaNexus] DharmaNexus database (matches for PA_atk-s05_09a) — Provides quantitative text-reuse matches across Pali literature, highlighting matches with the Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā, Apadāna-aṭṭhakathā, and individual therī-apadānas.
- [Norman, Philological Approach to Buddhism] K.R. Norman, A Philological Approach to Buddhism — Discusses canonization, commentarial control, and quotations of Therīgāthā-Apadāna in the commentary.
- [Silk 2009] Jonathan A. Silk, Riven by Lust: Incest and Schism in Indian Buddhist Legend and Historiography (2009) — Supplies bibliographic information on Pruitt's 1998 edition and translation of the commentary by Dhammapāla.
- [Skilling, Eṣā agrā] Peter Skilling, 'Eṣā agrā: Images of Nuns in (Mūla-)Sarvāstivādin Literature' — Characterizes the genre of the text, its authorship, modern edition and translation, and its treatment of nuns' ordination formulas.
